shared_elements: upright anthropomorphic monolith / pillar-like body carved in low relief
disc or oval motif on the upper body/chest area
horizontal register band with repeated vertical hatching (belt- or fringe-like)
curvilinear serpentine/limb-like elements descending from the shoulder area
row of repeated motifs across the top of the block
flat, schematic low-relief carving on a plain ground
justification: Both surfaces present a tall block treated as a body, with a horizontally banded hatched register crossing it like a belt or fringe, a disc/oval element set on the upper body, and sinuous relief forms running down from the shoulder region, all executed in flat schematic low relief on an otherwise blank ground. The decisive difference is content: A is dominated by human anatomy (head, hair, folded arms, hands meeting, pendant, V-shaped buckle) with almost no fauna, whereas B is populated by identifiable animals — a row of quadrupeds along the top, snakes, a crouching feline-headed creature and large birds — which A does not clearly show.
